learning: Iteration 6 showed slalom oscillation at 0.30 and s-bend at 0.304 with kd 0.55. The next race will show whether kd 0.60 keeps oscillation at or below 0.32 while mass and track tighten, and whether slalom max_error falls below 0.06. If oscillation rises, damping is still short; if max_error stays at 0.04 to 0.06 with stable oscillation, turn authority is the limit and kp needs a small rise.
notes: Geometry follows the Builder's iteration 7 proposal: mass 0.40 kg and wheel_track 0.11 m, with all other geometry unchanged. The controller raises kd from 0.55 to 0.60 to damp the faster turn response, and holds kp 3.8, ki 0.15 and base_speed 1.4.
rationale:
Iteration 6 (score 883.9) is the best design. Oval and s-bend both finish 20/20, and slalom finishes 14/20 with progress 0.94. Every agility step since iteration 3 has raised slalom progress without losing oval or s-bend completions. The remaining slalom failures are off_track endings with max_error at 0.04 on finishers, so the limit is turn response on alternating bends, not sensing or speed.

The Builder's iteration 7 geometry changes two things: mass 0.42 to 0.40 kg (about 5% lower yaw inertia) and wheel_track 0.115 to 0.11 m (about 4% more turn per unit of wheel differential). Both make the robot turn faster. Iteration 2 showed that kp 4.0 with kd 0.3 and a narrow track overshoots (steering_oscillation 0.27 to 0.28), and iteration 6 already sits at 0.30 on the slalom. So the extra agility needs more damping, not more gain.

Controller decisions: kp stays at 3.8, because the lower inertia and narrower track already add effective turn gain and raising kp would push oscillation further. kd rises from 0.55 to 0.60 to damp the faster heading response, a small step that follows the iteration 4 to 6 pattern where kd rose with each agility step and oscillation stayed at or below about 0.31. ki stays at 0.15 to cancel the fixed motor mismatch. base_speed stays at 1.4: the oval finishes in about 1.65 s and the slalom in about 2.0 s, so there is time margin, and changing speed would confound the geometry test. Sensor weights remain x/0.015, which keeps the signal sign-correct (positive = left). line_loss stays last_direction, which has produced about one event per run.

Expected result, not yet measured: slalom completions rise toward 16 of 20 or more, slalom steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.32, and oval and s-bend completions hold at 20/20 and 18/20 or better.
